Example Sentence: -(으)ㄹ (future modifier) + 것 (thing/fact) + 이다 (to be)
Sentence Translation: 우리가 가지고 있는 돈을 합치면 될 겁니다.
Etymology: It will work if we combine the money we have.

Part of Speech: I'm saying it is... / it means...
Example Sentence: -(이)라는 (that is called) + 말 (word/saying) + 이다 (to be)
Sentence Translation: 돌아가신 부모님께 물려받은 강이란 말이오!
Etymology: I’m saying this is a river I inherited from my late parents!

Example Sentence: Action verb + 는 (modifier) + 척 (pretending) + 하다 (to do)
Sentence Translation: 김선달은 고민하는 척하며 말했어요.
Etymology: Kim Seon-dal spoke while pretending to be deeply troubled.

Part of Speech: to be on the (adjective) side / relatively
Example Sentence: Modifier + 편 (side) + 이다 (to be)
Sentence Translation: 이 정도면 싼 편이오. 싫으면 마시오.
Etymology: At this level, it's on the cheap side. If you don't like it, forget it.

Example Sentence: -(으)ㄹ까 (wondering if) + 보다 (to see/consider)
Sentence Translation: 다른 사람에게 대동강을 팔까 봐 마음이 급해졌어요.
Etymology: Their hearts became hurried for fear that he might sell the Daedong River to someone else.

Example Sentence: 것 (act/thing) + 뿐 (only) + 이다 (to be)
Sentence Translation: 우리는 받은 돈을 다시 돌려준 것뿐입니다.
Etymology: We are only returning the money we received.

Example Sentence: 고 (connective particle)
Sentence Translation: 이미 김선달은 도망치고 없었어요.
Etymology: Kim Seon-dal had already fled and was gone.

Example Sentence: 아/어 (connective particle for cause/method)
Sentence Translation: 김선달은 대동강을 팔아 큰돈을 벌었어요.
Etymology: Kim Seon-dal made a lot of money by selling the Daedong River.

Part of Speech: it doesn't matter / to not care
Example Sentence: 상관 (relation/concern) + 없다 (to not exist)
Sentence Translation: 가지고 있는 돈을 다 써도 상관없다고 생각했어요.
Etymology: They thought it wouldn't matter even if they spent all the money they had.
